```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

A report that runs autonomously needs a predictable configuration: which R to use, which packages to prepare, where it can write, and which hosts it can contact.
This walkthrough builds that configuration in R, adds permissions, inspects both its complete and compact forms, and registers Console with an ellmer chat.
The chat writes report files and returns a summary that the surrounding job can send by email, for example as a daily sales update.

The examples are displayed without execution when this vignette is built.
To run them, choose an existing project directory containing your report data, replace the example domains with your services, and use a matching Console executable.
The final step also requires an ellmer provider and its credentials.

## Start with explicit settings

```{r paths}
library(mcp.console)

project <- normalizePath("/path/to/report", mustWork = TRUE)
binary <- Sys.which("mcp-console")
stopifnot(nzchar(binary))
```

Use the same `binary` and `project` for inspection and launch.
All relative configuration paths below are relative to `project`.
During development, set `binary` to the current checkout's executable; older releases may not support these configuration operations.

```{r config}
config <- ConsoleConfig(
  languages = "r",
  inherit_environment = FALSE,
  environment = c(TZ = "UTC"),
  r = RConfig(
    executable = current_r(),
    vanilla = TRUE,
    packages = c("rmarkdown", "httr2"),
    resolution = "startup_only"
  ),
  sandbox = SandboxPolicy(
    filesystem = SandboxFilesystem(
      read_only = "./data",
      read_write = "./reports",
      deny = path.expand("~/.ssh")
    ),
    network = SandboxNetwork(
      proxy = SandboxProxy(
        domains = SandboxDomains(allow = "api.example.com")
      )
    )
  )
)
```

`ConsoleConfig()` reads no configuration files, and passing this object to `console_tool()` skips global and project configuration discovery.
`current_r()` selects the installation running this script, including the Windows architecture directory and executable suffix.
Console starts a separate R session; `vanilla = TRUE` skips R startup files, and `startup_only` prepares the declared packages without allowing later package additions.

`inherit_environment = FALSE` excludes inherited worker and resolver environment variables; Console still supplies its owned runtime variables.
The launcher uses its trusted host environment to locate executables and prepare dependencies.
Configure provider credentials in the parent R process for ellmer; they are not forwarded to Console's workers unless you explicitly include them in the configuration.

## Add a writable directory and an allowed domain

S7 properties use `@`.
Append values to extend an existing grant:

```{r permissions}
config@sandbox@filesystem@read_write <- c(
  config@sandbox@filesystem@read_write,
  "./figures"
)
config@sandbox@network@proxy@domains@allow <- c(
  config@sandbox@network@proxy@domains@allow,
  "data.example.com"
)

for (directory in config@sandbox@filesystem@read_write) {
  destination <- file.path(project, directory)
  if (!dir.exists(destination)) {
    stopifnot(dir.create(destination, recursive = TRUE))
  }
}
```

Create writable directories before launching Console.
The filesystem policy retains Console's host-read baseline: `read_only = "./data"` does not hide other readable host files.
Use `deny` for sensitive locations.
Proxy rules allow hostnames or IP patterns; they do not constrain URL paths or email recipients.

Dependency preparation has separate permissions and may download packages.
See [Resolver configuration](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/mcp-console/RESOLVER.html) when preparation needs a different policy; explicit resolver sandbox policies are unsupported on Windows.

## Inspect the complete and compact configurations

```{r inspect}
full <- materialize_console_config(config, path = binary, project = project)
print(full)

compact <- prune_console_config(full, path = binary, project = project)
print(compact)
```

Both results are ordinary, editable `ConsoleConfig` objects.
`full` includes native defaults, the tool description, and parameter descriptions and schema metadata.
`compact` shows settings that differ from those defaults, retaining meaningful empty values.
These operations validate configuration without starting interpreters or installing packages.

Review the permissions and generated tool guidance before launch.
Printing a config includes its configured environment values, so inspect it before adding secrets if the output will be shared.
For structural comparisons, use `as.list(full)`, `as.list(compact)`, or `all.equal()` on two such lists.

Launch `full` to keep its materialized defaults and descriptions.
Launching `compact` instead lets omitted settings follow the defaults of the selected Console binary.
Neither form locks package versions or snapshots the host environment.
If you later edit permissions or parameter visibility in `full`, set affected tool descriptions to `NULL` before materializing again so Console can regenerate them.

## Launch the report

```{r launch}
send <- console_tool(config = full, path = binary, project = project)

chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(
  system_prompt = paste(
    "Use the console to prepare the scheduled report.",
    "Read input files from data/ and write the report to reports/.",
    "Write figures to figures/ and explain any missing inputs."
  )
)
chat$register_tool(send)
summary <- chat$chat(
  paste(
    "Summarize the latest data in data/sales.csv.",
    "Save reports/sales-summary.md and a sales trend plot in figures/.",
    "Return a short summary and the paths of the files you created."
  )
)
cat(summary)
```

Replace the input filename and task with your report's requirements.
The permission policy is enforced by Console; the prompt describes the task.
Keep `send` and `chat` reachable until the job finishes.
Your surrounding R script can deliver the summary or report through its existing email workflow, with the recipient specified in that script.

Save the code in a script such as `report.R` and have your scheduler run `Rscript --vanilla report.R`.
For scheduled runs, the R installation that runs that script is the one selected by `current_r()`.
You can save an inspected configuration with `saveRDS(full, "report-config.rds")` and load it with `readRDS()`; continue to supply the intended `binary` and `project` at launch.

For a workflow that starts from files, use `discover_console_config()` to read optional global/project files explicitly, or `read_console_config()` to require one JSON or YAML file.
See `?config-workflow` for those operations and `?console_tool` for launch options.
